description: One node in a scene file: add, read, set, duplicate, reparent or delete it, or paint TileMap cells. Any ClassDB node type can be added, so a NavigationRegion2D, an AnimationTree or a Camera3D is an add with that nodeType and its properties, and another scene is instanced by an add with instancePath. set with name renames a node. A property holding a Resource takes the res:// path of one, so a texture, a material or a theme is a set like any other. A write is refused while the editor holds unsaved changes to the scene, and for a node that belongs to a scene this one instances or inherits. Needs the editor connected. Operations: add (needs nodeName): add a node of any class, or an instance of a scene; get (needs nodePath): read a node's properties, and a TileMapLayer's or TileMap's cells as set_tilemap_cells takes them, the first 1000 with cellCount for all; set (needs nodePath, properties): set properties on a node; duplicate (needs nodePath, newName): copy a node and its children; reparent (needs nodePath, newParentPath): move a node under another parent, or to another place among its siblings; delete (needs nodePath): remove a node and its children; set_tilemap_cells (needs nodePath, cells): place tiles in a TileMapLayer or TileMap.

includeDefaults.description: get: include properties still at their default. Default false.

index.description: add and reparent: where the node goes among the parent's children, 0 for first. Default last. Child order is draw order in a CanvasItem and layout order in a Container. Only for ops add, reparent.

instancePath.description: add: a scene to instance as the new node instead of a class, such as "ui/panel.tscn". It is saved as an instance of that file, the way the editor's Instantiate Child Scene saves one, so changes to that scene reach it; properties set its root. A scene that is the target or instances it is refused. Only for op add.

layer.description: set_tilemap_cells: the layer of a TileMap. Default 0. A TileMapLayer is one layer.

newParentPath.description: reparent: the new parent, which may be the one it has, to move it among its siblings.

nodePath.description: Node path from the scene root, such as "Player/Sprite2D". "." is the root.

nodeType.description: add: the node class, such as "CharacterBody2D". Give this or instancePath.

parentNodePath.description: add: where the node goes. Default the root. duplicate: where the copy goes.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project directory, the one holding project.godot.

properties.description: Properties to set, keyed by Godot property name. Vectors, colours and the like may be written as {"x": 1, "y": 2} or tagged {"_type": "Vector2", "x": 1, "y": 2}, which is the form a read answers with, so a value read off one node can be written straight to another. A key may also be a colon path into one of the components of a vector, a colour, a rectangle or a transform, as GDScript names them, so one axis is written alone: "position:x", "modulate:a", "region_rect:size:y"; a component the value does not have is refused, naming the ones it has. A property holding a node takes the path to it from the node being set, such as "../Player". Each value is read back once set, and one the engine changed or refused is refused with what it holds.

scenePath.description: Scene file inside the project, such as "scenes/main.tscn" or "res://scenes/main.tscn".

name: scene_node
title: Scene nodes
